Loved Turtles in Time, but this always did confuse me:
Why did Playstation All Stars Battle Royale fail tremendously compared to SSB?
The name's a lot worse for one. How do you think the game play compares to SSB overall? The balance? The overall presentation, polish and characters chosen?

I'm going to assume it's based upon mechanics.

Smash:

  • K.O. your opponent until no stocks remain/time runs out/both
  • Losing a life can be a result of an "Ultimate", high damage, environment, et cetera
  • "Ultimate" attack ability given by chance, doesn't always OHKO

Battle Royale:

  • Last one left standing
  • Losing a life usually a result of an ultimate
  • "Ultimate" move acquired over time through damage, always OHKO

It could also be argued that Sony has less memorable characters, as Nintendo has been around for a while and almost everyone can recognize their flagship characters almost immediately. Plus the whole "copycat" mindset some people have for whatever reason.

I've never heard "I wanna see Nathan Drake beat the shit out of Big Boss!", but I've heard "I want to falcon punch Duck Hunt Dog's face in."

I think the character selection was one of the worse things about PSAS. The two biggest downsides were that Capcom made them use DmC Dante, and Activision wouldn't let them use Crash or Spyro. Using Raiden over Snake was an interesting choice as well, but Raiden still represented the MGS series better than Neo-Dante did DMC. My only other real complaints regarding character is that they gave Cole (inFamous) two slots and the inclusion of Big Daddy (BioShock). I think Nintendo just has more memorable characters than Playstation, and this along with the characters chosen just made it less fun.

As for gameplay: it's good, but they tried too hard to be both a "serious" fighting game and a party game all at once, so it ended up being great at neither. Still worth the $15 I spent on it though, it was a decent time. I'd definitely rent or buy cheap if they made another.

I think it just comes down to the roster. Sony franchises simply aren't that memorable. Nintendo games are story-light but character-heavy, and getting to play with all those different characters in one giant cluster-fuck of a fighting game is fun. And they're all of a similar type, with varying levels of cartoony. And they, for the most part, have 20+ years of franchise history.

Sony and a man who fights with fists, and a man with electric powers, and a man with a gun, and a man with a sword, and a man with a sword and a gun, and three of those five are third-party characters. And the man with electric powers has a clone to pad the roster. Nintendo has clone characters too, but that's in a roster of 40-plus. Sony had a dozen, and they were still scratching for decent characters to fill the roster.
